name: Food safety
what: Meet the Food Standards Code, register or license the food business, appoint a food safety supervisor where required, and be inspected.

layers.who: Food Standards Australia New Zealand (the Food Standards Code)
State food authority or health department (higher-risk businesses)
State food authority or health department
Local council (registration of retail and food service businesses)

consistency_note: One national food code, adopted by each state's food law; registration, licensing and inspection are run differently by each state and by councils.

basis.source: Accommodation and food services industry (industry information)
basis.quote: All food sold, processed or handled for sale in Australia and New Zealand must comply with the Food Standards Code .

basis.source: Performance Benchmarking of Australian and New Zealand Business Regulation: Food Safety
basis.quote: Local councils play a key role in the administration and enforcement of consumer food safety regulation, except in the Australian territories.

issues.what: Councils enforce food safety for most food businesses, and differ in fees, inspection frequency and enforcement.

evidence.source: Performance Benchmarking of Australian and New Zealand Business Regulation: Food Safety
evidence.quote: There are significant differences in councils' fees and charges, inspection rates, enforcement practices and transparency of their activities, which can lead to unnecessary burdens on business.

issues.what: Some food businesses are inspected by their council and audited again by a state regulator for the same food safety matters.

evidence.source: Performance Benchmarking of Australian and New Zealand Business Regulation: Food Safety
evidence.quote: the overlap and duplication of inspection requirements (sub. 10) - for example, butchers being inspected by the local council and then being audited (or inspected) on food safety matters by other regulators

issues.what: Businesses report that environmental health officers interpret the same food laws differently.

evidence.source: Performance Benchmarking of Australian and New Zealand Business Regulation: Food Safety
evidence.quote: criticisms from food business interests centred around issues of inconsistent interpretation and implementation of food laws by environmental health and similarly authorised officers

issues.what: States differed on whether food businesses must have a food safety supervisor or a food safety plan.

evidence.source: Performance Benchmarking of Australian and New Zealand Business Regulation: Food Safety
evidence.quote: The most significant difference occurs over requirements to employ a food safety supervisor and to prepare a food safety plan.
Food service, caterer and related retail businesses in Australia need to meet food safety requirements that came in December 2023.

issues.status_note: A national standard requiring food safety supervisors in food service, catering and retail took effect in December 2023 (FSANZ).
